stories.title: Mowi posts record Q3 revenue and raises its 2026 and 2027 harvest guidance.
stories.summary: Q3 revenue was a record EUR 1.73 billion on 186,000 tonnes harvested, and operating profit rose 146%. 2026 guidance went up 20,000 tonnes to 620,000 tonnes, with 630,000 tonnes guided for 2027, of which Chile contributes 88,000 tonnes. The quarterly dividend is NOK 2.30 per share (about NOK 1.2 billion), and Q4 contract coverage is 17% in Norway and 23% in Chile. SEB, Fearnley and Arctic kept Buy ratings, and Mowi calls itself the world's largest seafood company.

stories.title: SalMar beats expectations with record harvest and doubled operating profit in Q3.
stories.summary: Operational EBIT was NOK 1.61 billion against NOK 711 million a year earlier, on a record 105,100 tonnes harvested (up 13%). Guidance for harvest volumes is below expectations, with lower Norwegian volumes forecast for Q4 and September issues carrying into the quarter. SalMar sees 347,000 tonnes in 2026 and 348,000 in 2027, and analysts were split on the outlook.

stories.summary: Operational EBIT was DKK 128m against DKK 22m a year earlier, helped by strong Faroese biology and feed earnings, but Finansavisen put expectations at DKK 228m. top.why: Mowi raised 2026 harvest guidance by 20,000 tonnes to 620,000 tonnes and guided 630,000 tonnes for 2027, on record Q3 revenue and a 146% rise in operating profit.
Peru's ENFEN expects the extraordinary coastal El Niño to last until February 2027 and persist to late autumn 2027, a key risk for the anchovy supply behind fishmeal and fish oil.

Agrosuper signed a memorandum to buy Blumar's salmon business for up to US$540 million, which would create the world's second-largest producer, and Multi X is reportedly exploring a purchase of Ventisqueros.
Bakkafrost's Q3 operational EBIT of DKK 128m missed expectations, and it sees global supply falling 3% in Q4 while Scottish losses continue.
SalMar posted a record 105,100-tonne Q3 harvest and doubled operating profit, but guided to lower Norwegian volumes in Q4 and 347,000 tonnes for 2026, below expectations.
